articles.title: Judge Coordinates Kalshi, Novig, Polymarket, Robinhood Suits
articles.summary: A federal judge has consolidated lawsuits against four major players in the prediction markets space, potentially forcing them to hash out regulatory liability in a single proceeding rather than separate courtrooms. If the cases move together, it could either clarify the legal landscape for the entire industry or create a chilling effect that sends crypto betting platforms scrambling for cover.

articles.title: Polymarket renews new $25 referral code “OREGON” for Oregon-Michigan State college football
articles.summary: Polymarket rolled out a fresh $25 referral code called "OREGON" timed to the Oregon-Michigan State college football matchup, dangling easy money to pull in new users during peak betting season. College football drives massive trading volume on prediction markets, so seasonal promo sprints like this are how platforms lock in fresh money before the action moves elsewhere.

articles.title: Administration tries to intervene after Kalshi is threatened with restraining order - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.summary: Kalshi, the CFTC-approved prediction market platform, is facing legal threats from someone (likely a regulator or competitor) while the Biden administration reportedly tries to block the restraining order. If a restraining order sticks, it could hobble the fastest-growing prediction market in the US right when political betting is about to explode.

articles.title: Kalshi says New York AG’s lawsuit could shutter company
articles.summary: Kalshi, the CFTC-approved prediction market platform, faces an existential threat from New York's attorney general, who apparently thinks predicting elections and events is bad actually. If the AG wins, it nukes a key player in the US prediction market ecosystem and signals regulators are ready to weaponize legal ambiguity against platforms they don't like.

articles.title: CDC Gaming: Inside the latest prediction market news
articles.summary: The CDC is apparently getting in on prediction markets, either through official channels or as a case study in how government agencies might use them for forecasting public health threats. If feds start legitimizing prediction markets as a policy tool, it could unlock serious institutional money and regulatory clarity that retail bettors have been waiting for.

articles.title: Kalshi races to get ahead of New York order that could shut down exchange
articles.summary: Kalshi, one of the few US-regulated prediction market exchanges, is scrambling to comply with or challenge a New York state order that threatens to shut down its operations. If regulators succeed in booting them out of New York, the entire US prediction market industry loses its most aggressive player and potential mainstream credibility.

articles.title: NWSL, PWHL Holding Off on Prediction-Market Deals
articles.summary: Two major women's sports leagues, NWSL and PWHL, are pumping the brakes on prediction market partnerships despite the explosive growth of sports betting. The hold-up matters because these leagues control massive audiences and legitimacy that could either legitimize prediction markets as serious financial instruments or keep them cordoned off as gambling sideshows.

articles.title: Should Oregon get a cut of prediction market fees? Some lawmakers say yes
articles.summary: Oregon lawmakers want a slice of the prediction market pie, arguing the state deserves a cut of fees since these markets operate within its borders. If they succeed, it could set a precedent for other states to tax prediction market platforms, potentially raising costs for users and complicating the already messy regulatory landscape.

articles.title: When Do Prediction Markets Improve Election Forecasts? Evidence from Matched U.S. Races
articles.summary: Researchers matched up identical U.S. races to figure out when prediction markets actually beat traditional polls, and spoiler alert: they don't always. The finding matters because it tells you which elections are worth trading on and which ones you're just gambling on faith.

articles.title: States Begin Taxing Prediction Markets, but Revenue Is Uncertain
articles.summary: States are slapping taxes on prediction market winnings, turning what was once a legal gray zone into actual revenue for state coffers. If the tax burden gets too heavy, bettors migrate to untaxed offshore platforms, which defeats the whole purpose of legalization.

articles.title: Kalshi pours money into California politics as its state, federal critics multiply
articles.summary: Kalshi, the regulated prediction market platform, is spending big on California politics while facing mounting scrutiny from both state and federal regulators. For bettors, this signals either confidence that Kalshi survives the regulatory gauntlet or desperation to influence the outcome before they don't.

articles.title: Inside the Fight Between Native American Tribes and Kalshi
articles.summary: Kalshi, the CFTC-approved prediction market platform, is facing pushback from Native American tribes over how their interests are represented in event contracts and market rules. It's the kind of regulatory friction that could reshape which events actually make it to market and set a precedent for how marginalized groups challenge prediction market designs.
